name: Fund Performance and Attribution

positioning.oneLineSummary: Separates realized cash, unrealized marks, return multiples, timing, benchmark, deal contribution, and team attribution before claiming fund skill.
positioning.productLabel: Fund Performance Lens — product synthesis anchored to Ramsinghani's performance-analysis chapter
notAClaimOf: one successful deal proving repeatable skill

attribution.display: Product synthesis anchored to Mahendra Ramsinghani's third-edition performance-analysis chapter

neutralParaphrase: Evaluate fund and investor performance with multiple complementary views: invested and distributed cash, residual value, timing, vintage and benchmark context, company concentration, source and decision attribution, and realized versus unrealized status. State uncertainty and data limitations before inferring repeatable edge.

locator.value: Public summary identifying rate of return and cash-on-cash return as primary measures
Chapter 14 pp. 137-153; metric definitions and attribution pending lawful review
Public summary: performance, team stability, and strategy consistency in LP diligence

requiredConditions: Cash flows, valuations, dates, fees, carry, and ownership are consistently defined.
Realized and unrealized results remain separate.
Benchmark and vintage choices are disclosed.
Attribution distinguishes sourcing, selection, ownership, support, timing, and luck without overstating causality.

requiredEvidence.description: Dated contributions, distributions, NAV, valuation policy, fees, carry, and currency.
Investments, follow-ons, proceeds, marks, source, sponsor, decision record, and ownership by deal.
Vintage, geography, stage, strategy, public-market cash-flow benchmark, and methodology.

decisionQuestions: How much value is realized versus marked?
What do multiple and timing measures each reveal?
Which companies drive the result and how concentrated is it?
What benchmark and vintage are appropriate?
Which team members sourced, led, followed on, and supported each outcome?
What evidence supports repeatable edge rather than outcome luck?
positiveSignals: Cash flows and NAV reconcile to audited records.
Realized and unrealized contributions are separate.
Multiple timing and benchmark views agree directionally.
Deal and team attribution has contemporaneous records.
Edge claims survive losses and missed-deal analysis.
redFlags: IRR is shown without cash-flow timing or multiple.
Marked-up private rounds are treated as distributions.
A top deal hides weak remaining portfolio performance.
Benchmark or vintage is selected after seeing the result.
Attribution credits only successes and ignores misses.
disconfirmingEvidence: Results are dominated by one unrealized mark.
Public-market equivalent or matched vintage reverses the conclusion.
Winning deals came through unrepeatable access.
Team attribution records conflict with current claims.
contraindications: Do not infer future returns from past performance alone.
Do not conflate gross and net performance.
Do not treat NAV as cash.
Do not publish author-attributed metric rules before Chapter 14 review.

instructions: Normalize dated fund and deal cash flows.
Separate realized, unrealized, gross, and net views.
Compare with disclosed benchmark and vintage.
Produce deal/team attribution with uncertainty and counterevidence.

sourceReliability.medium: Administrator data exists but marks or attribution are unaudited.
sourceReliability.high: Audited cash flows, policy-consistent marks, and contemporaneous attribution records reconcile.

evidenceStrength.low: One metric or one deal drives the claim.
evidenceStrength.medium: Multiple views agree but realizations or benchmarks are limited.
evidenceStrength.high: Realized results, benchmarks, and repeated attribution support the conclusion.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only gross IRR or TVPI is available.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Fund metrics are complete but deal attribution or benchmark is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Cash flows, marks, gross/net, benchmarks, deals, team, misses, and vintage are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: Fund vehicle or cash flows are incompatible with the metric set.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Vehicle, currency, vintage, and benchmark are normalized.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Performance can be described but repeatability remains uncertain.
judgmentConfidence.high: A bounded, evidence-based edge claim is defensible.

promotionRequirements: Validate metric definitions with fund administrators and LPs.
empiricalQualifications: Private valuations are subjective and stale.
Team attribution is observational and can be politically biased.

rights.notes: Public sources establish topic and high-level objectives; detailed metric and attribution rules await licensed review.
